content.text: A web service architecture that uses standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, etc.) to interact with resources identified by URIs.
A framework built on top of Spring that simplifies the development of Java-based enterprise applications by providing embedded servers, auto-configuration, and a range of starter dependencies.
A Spring annotation that combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, marking the class as a REST endpoint.
Annotations used to map HTTP requests to handler methods.

sections.heading: Creating a RESTful Web Service (Exposing API)

items: Open STS and import the existing project InfyGoBoot_YAML. Rename it to InfyGoBoot_RESTService_WithoutSecurity.
Add package: com.infosys.irs.api
@RestController → Class handles REST requests.
@PathVariable → Extracts values from the URI.
ResponseEntity → Wraps the response with HTTP status.
Right-click project > Run As > Spring Boot App
Visit Spring Initializr
Select Maven, Spring Boot, switch to full version
Add dependencies: Spring Web, Thymeleaf, etc.
Generate and unzip the project
Import into STS and rename to: InfyGoBoot_RESTClient_WithoutSecurity

items: Place static assets (css, js, imgs) in: src/main/resources/static
Place JSP pages (searchFlights.jsp, header.jsp, etc.) in: src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/pages
Run project: Right-click > Run As > Spring Boot App
Visit: http://localhost:4848/InfyGoBootRestClient/flight
Fill Origin, Destination, and Journey Date
Click Search Flights and view results
Spring Boot simplifies REST API development.
Use @RestController for exposing endpoints.
Use RestTemplate for consuming APIs.
Configure the view layer with JSPs and static assets.
Bootstrap the application using Spring Boot’s embedded server.
